## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to add observability with minimal surface area using existing CNF sidecars and Kubernetes ConfigMaps. It assesses understanding of multi-tenant security boundaries and metrics cardinality management.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant labeling in Prometheus metrics
- Prometheus text format exposition
- ConfigMap-based feature flags and sampling control
- High-cardinality label management

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-metrics-config
  namespace: tenant-namespace
data:
  cnf.metrics.enabled: 'true'
  cnf.metrics.endpoint: '/metrics'
  cnf.metrics.sample-rate: '0.5'
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-namespace
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-metrics-config
  namespace: tenant-namespace
data:
  cnf.metrics.enabled: 'true'
  cnf.metrics.endpoint: '/metrics'
  cnf.metrics.sample-rate: '0.5'
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-namespace
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: cnf-gateway:latest
      - name: metrics-sidecar
        image: metrics-sidecar:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
          name: metrics
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle high-cardinality label explosion with many tenants and paths?
- How would you verify no tenant data cross-contamination occurs in metrics?
- How does the sampling rate affect metric accuracy and Prometheus storage?

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses ability to design end-to-end supply chain security and runtime integrity for multi-cloud CNFs, including identity management, attestation mechanisms, policy-as-code enforcement, and network isolation during zero-downtime upgrades.

## Key Concepts
- SPIFFE/SPIRE identity management
- TPM/IMA runtime attestation
- SPDX SBOM delta validation
- OPA/Kyverno policy enforcement
- Cilium eBPF network policies
- Canary upgrade strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
# SPIFFE identity configuration
apiVersion: spiffe.example/v1
kind: SPIFFEIdentity
metadata:
  name: cnf-identity-01
spec:
  spiffeID: spiffe://cluster/ns/cnf-01
  parentID: spiffe://cluster/ns/workload-scheduler
  ttl: 1h
```

```yaml
# OPA upgrade gate policy
package cnf.upgrade
default allow = false

allow {
  input.attestation.trust_score >= 80
  input.sbom.delta.additions == 0
  input.network_policy.isolated == true
}
```

## Implementation Approach
The solution integrates identity, attestation, and policy enforcement to ensure upgrades maintain security posture while achieving zero downtime through controlled canary deployments.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement multi-tenant zero-trust mTLS using SPIFFE IDs, short-lived cert rotation, and KMS-backed CA in CNF gateways.

## Key Concepts
- SPIFFE/SPIRE trust domains per tenant
- CSR-based certificate rotation with short lifetimes
- Per-tenant mesh policies (Istio/OPA) for north-south and east-west traffic
- Workload identity verification via SPIFFE IDs

## Code Example
```yaml
# CSR bootstrap (outline)
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-td1-csr
spec:
  signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-clientSigner
  request: <base64-csr>
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
```

```yaml
# Per-tenant policy (outline)
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-td1-gateway
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["spiffe://td1/ns/default/sa/gateway"]
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET","POST"]
```

- How would you handle cert revocation in case of a compromised gateway?
- How would you test cross-tenant isolation under peak load?

## Why This Is Asked

This question probes practical rollout discipline, end-to-end image provenance, and tenant isolation during CNF upgrades. It requires concrete mechanisms for per‑tenant traffic shaping, SBOM enforcement, and reliable rollback in production.

## Key Concepts

- Canary deployments with tenant segmentation
- Image provenance with Cosign signing and SBOM validation
- Per-tenant traffic routing and gradual rollout
- Telemetry driven rollback thresholds and auditability

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal canary deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway-canary
  namespace: cnf
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
        canary: "true"
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: registry.example.com/cnf/gateway:canary
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        env:
        - name: TENANT_ROUTES
          value: "tenant-a,tenant-b"
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test canary routing for late joiners without affecting existing tenants?
- What metrics and alerting would you use to distinguish occasional outliers from genuine SLO breaches during canary?
